qs.q: A 58-year-old male presents with acute substernal chest pain. Coronary angiography reveals an occluded left anterior descending artery. Which of the following represents the earliest ultrastructural and microscopic change expected in the myocardium within the first 24 hours?
o: Granulation tissue formation in the infarct
Neutrophil infiltration into the ischemic area
Coagulative necrosis of the myocardial tissue
Collagen scar deposition replacing the tissue
qs.e: Coagulative necrosis is the earliest microscopic change seen within the first 24 hours of a myocardial infarction. Neutrophil infiltration occurs subsequently between 1 to 3 days.
